references.text: Only male descendants of Aaron, the priests, shall eat from the sin offering. This verse confirms that only male priests could eat from the holy offerings.
The priest who presents the sin offering shall eat it in a holy place, in the court of the tent of meeting. This elaborates on the requirement that the offering must be eaten in a holy place.
The guilt offering is most holy, just as described in verse 6. This establishes the context for the holiness of the guilt offering.
What remains of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons as most holy. Shows that priests have the right to eat from the most holy offerings.
Moses instructs Aaron and his surviving sons to eat the grain offering in a holy place, because it is most holy. Confirms the practice of priests eating holy food offerings.
A priest with a defect may eat from his God's food, both from the most holy and the holy. Shows that male priests had the right to eat from the holy offerings.
The most holy portion that is not burned belongs to the priests and shall be eaten in a holy place by all men. Confirms the rule that only male priests may eat the most holy food offerings.
Ezekiel's vision describes that the priests shall eat the most holy offerings in a holy place. Shows the continuity of the rules for the priests' meals in the temple.
